These are indubitably Shoshonean, but not of any known dialect nor wholly of affiliation with any one dialect group.. the vanishing trace of a distinctive Shoshonean language and group. sources.note: Nothing. The entire Giamina record is a 20-word list on p. 128 (tcupu 'house', hewe 'water', pohoim 'road', wadja 'mountain', madjindji 'across', pābahai 'no', xöxinil/xaxinil 'person', muut 'man', wi'ct 'woman', piāt 'deer', ni-ku, bal/bal-aku, bèkt, tabakwan, dab-iku, hahītcu/ahītciwa, em 'much', hüüka 'drink', mik'an 'kill'; numerals 1-6). Page image checked: vowel diacritics only, no accent marks. The words 'accent' and 'stress' do not occur anywhere in the text layer of the whole 1907 monograph; the general phonetic note (pp. 96-100) concerns consonant classes and the ö/ü vowels.
